8-915A. Military Occupational Specialty 915A--Automotive Maintenance Warrant Officer (Effective
202510)
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. None
    b. Prerequisites. AR 135-100, DA Pam 601-6, and DA Pam 611-21.
    c. MOS 915A. MOS 915A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOSs are 91A, 91B, 91C, 91D,
91H, 91J, 91L, 91M, 91P, 91S, 91X, and 91Z.
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) T--Transition
        (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASIs associated with all warrant
officer MOS)).
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Complete the Automotive Maintenance Warrant Officer Basic Course.
               (b) Have correctable vision, normal color discrimination, normal hearing, and full use of upper
and lower extremities per AR 40-501.
         (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(1).
               (b) Complete the Automotive Maintenance Warrant Officer Advanced Course.
         (3) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f(2).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
         (4) CW5 must--see MOS 915E.
    g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2--
               (a) Plans, organizes, and allocates resources and facilities to execute maintenance and
repair of light and heavy military and commercial wheeled vehicles; wheeled construction equipment;
mobile electric power generation; armament systems; small arms; fire control; ground support equipment
and power-driven chemical equipment.
               (b) Evaluates and inspects maintenance operations and develops and implements corrective
action plans where necessary to comply with regulatory and statutory requirements applicable to
industrial maintenance operations in fixed facilities or field environments.
               (c) Identifies technical training deficiencies within the military or civilian work force and
develops comprehensive corrective action plans to provide necessary training. Personally trains
maintenance personnel to accurately diagnose/troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, pneumatic and
hydraulic malfunctions accurately using the latest test equipment, technical publications and procedures
available.
               (d) Provides management oversight and technical guidance on the establishment of unit
Shop Stock, Bench Stock, and consumable shop supplies per applicable supply calculations.
Coordinates for, or provides technical training for Army Logistics Information Systems (LIS) system
operators.
               (e) Develops and updates the commander’s Standing Operating Procedures (SOP) for the
conduct of maintenance operations to include: safety, fire prevention and environmental protection and
physical security within the maintenance facility. Assist the commander in preparation for all external
inspections and visits by installation/ACOM safety, fire prevention, and environmental protection
agencies.
               (f) Oversees the commander’s calibration program and ensures calibration operations are
treated as maintenance operations and are covered in the unit’s maintenance SOP.
               (g) Oversees the Army Oil Analysis Program to ensure it is in compliance with regulatory
requirements.
               (h) Trains and directs recovery vehicle operators in safe and correct recovery operations.
               (i) Utilizes LIS to provide maintenance and readiness information to the commander and
supervisors. Submits Software Engineering Change Proposals to the appropriate agencies when
automated maintenance management systems do not function as designed.
              (j) Plans, schedules, and publishes scheduled service plans for all assigned equipment per
the applicable technical manuals/lubrication orders.
              (k) Coordinates with the installation/ACOM or AMC, on application of modification work
orders on unit equipment.
              (l) Conducts technical inspections of unit equipment to determine maintenance status. This
includes CBRN, weapons, communications, ground support equipment, and required sets, kits, outfits,
and tools (SKOT).
              (m) Manages property accountability for the commander for all equipment used in the
performance of maintenance.
              (n) Ensures that maintenance personnel are using current technical publications. Inspects
and verifies that pinpoint distribution accounts are current for all maintenance sections in the unit.
              (o) Establishes the commander’s quality assurance program for maintenance and repairs.
Oversee all quality control inspections and inspectors to validate their capability to identify improper
repairs and scheduled services.
              (p) Acts as the commander’s Command Inspection Program (CIP) maintenance team chief.
Personally ensures that the CIP is fair and inspecting to the published standard in all areas associated
with equipment maintenance.
              (q) Coordinates with other maintenance activities and external agencies to resolve
disagreements and maintenance quality control problems.
              (r) Acts as the unit point of contact for Army Materiel Status System (AMSS) reporting and
issues that arise between the unit, the support operations/distribution management center and Army
level.
       (2) CW3
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
              (b) Serves as the senior technical advisor to battalion commanders and the staffs of combat
arms maneuver battalions, forward support companies, and task organized combat arms maneuver
formations.
              (c) Assists a combat arms maneuver battalion or forward support company staff in the
planning, coordination, and execution of maintenance support during tactical training and combat
operations.
              (d) Provides technical expertise in maintenance doctrine on the battlefield necessary for a
combat maneuver battalion or squadron staff to efficiently employ maintenance personnel and equipment
in support of the commander’s mission.
              (e) Coordinates maintenance support necessary for sustainment of readiness in a combat
arms maneuver battalion or squadron.
              (f) Provides input to supporting maintenance unit commanders and their staffs on tactical
support requirements peculiar to the combat maneuver battalion or squadron.
              (g) Directs and manages field level automotive, and related support equipment repair teams,
sections, and platoons in forward support companies, support maintenance companies, and other
combat service support units.
              (h) Controls work flow in field maintenance shops under his/her control.
              (i) Trains maintainers in correct diagnostics, repair, and quality control procedures on
equipment repaired in shops under his/her control.
              (j) Establishes internal controls for requesting, maintaining, and properly disposing of
supplies, tools and parts, and technical reference material within shops under his/her control.
              (k) Provides input to the commander for development of internal and external maintenance
Standing Operating Procedures (SOP).
              (l) Provides technical advice to the commander on the efficient employment of field repair
capability in field training and combat environments.
              (m) Employs automated maintenance management systems to improve productivity in shops
under his/her control.
              (n) Provides technical advice to supported unit commanders and staff on technical
maintenance management and maintenance doctrine.
             (o) Acts as installation, Army Command, or Army maintenance inspection or training team
chief.
             (p) Diagnoses complex malfunctions on automotive and support equipment when the
malfunctions are beyond the capability of subordinates.
             (q) Provides Ordnance related technical and doctrinal expertise to brigade and group level
commanders and staffs.                                     .
        (3) CW4.
             (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1) and g(2).
             (b) Serves as the senior ground maintenance technical advisor in brigade and group levels of
command.
             (c)Assists brigade and group staff in the planning, coordination, and execution of
maintenance support.
             (d) Provides technical expertise in maintenance doctrine on the battlefield for brigade and
subordinate element level commanders and staff to efficiently employ maintenance personnel and
equipment in support of the commanders’ mission.
             (e) Manages materiel readiness reporting for brigade and echelons above brigade
organizations.
             (f) Performs materiel readiness management duties at sustainment brigade and sustainment
command levels.
             (g) Performs research, development, test and evaluation duties.
             (h) Assists in coordination and evaluates maintenance performed by contract support.
             (i) Serves as Ordnance technical subject matter expert in training, capability, and materiel
development positions.
             (j) Advises commanders on the progression and utilization of subordinate Ordnance warrant
officers.               (4) CW5 see MOS 915E.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
        (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
        (2) A minimum OPAT score of (Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) -
0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles) is required in
Physical Demand Category “Moderate” (Gold).
        (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2
equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the
following standards of grade tables:
             (a) Table 8-915A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
             (b) Table 8-915A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations.
